title: Choosing between a fillet weld and a bolted joint
prompt: A bracket must carry a fluctuating shear load and may need to be removed for service. Compare a fillet-welded joint with a bolted joint and say which you would choose and why.
sourceNote: Original example question written for the import documentation.
idealAnswer: Welds give a continuous, stiff joint but create residual stress and heat-affected zones that hurt fatigue life, and they are permanent. Bolted joints allow disassembly, and a properly preloaded joint keeps the load in friction so the bolt sees little cyclic load, which helps fatigue; they need hole tolerances, preload control and anti-loosening measures. For a fluctuating load that needs service access, choose a preloaded bolted joint, and verify slip resistance and bearing stress.

rubric.name: Technical accuracy
rubric.description: Correctly compares welded and bolted joints for fatigue and serviceability.
expectedConcepts: welds create residual stress and heat-affected zones
preload keeps load in friction and reduces cyclic bolt load
alternatives: Fatigue-rated weld details can work with post-weld treatment
misconceptions: Welds are always stronger than bolts
